subject: Media Literacy
title: Messengers and the Speed of News
description: A micro-lesson that makes Messengers and the Speed of News usable.

hook.text: In the ancient world, news traveled at the speed of a horse — about 30 miles per day.

buildup.text: Empires built relay systems: Persia's Royal Road, Rome's cursus publicus, China's postal routes.

discovery.text: Faster messaging meant faster governance. The empire that communicated fastest often won wars.

twist.text: For thousands of years, the speed of communication barely changed. A horse in 500 BCE was still top speed in 1800.

climax.text: The telegraph in 1844 shattered this barrier, making news instant for the first time.

punchline.text: For 5,000 years, news moved at horse speed.

quiz.question: What technology first made news transmission nearly instant?
